title: POC weekly sync - reliability incident follow-up
summary: Weekly POC sync to review this week's reliability incidents: intermittent 5xxs, timeouts, and client-side rate-limiting. SE walked through server logs and retry/backoff tuning. Agreed next steps: run extended load test with 1.2x traffic profile, enable request-level tracing, adjust client retry policy and token bucket limits, and follow up with post-test dashboard and incident playbook update.
topics: Incident timeline and root cause hypotheses
KV cache and prefix cache 영향 (mis-transcribed)
Dedicated vs hosted routing under burst
next_steps: Redwood to share updated retry guidance doc and sample client config (by 2026-04-27)
Nimbus to run extended load test and share traces (by 2026-05-01)
Schedule deep-dive on VPC network path with Nimbus infra (by 2026-05-04)
Redwood SE to enable request-level tracing for pilot and send dashboard link
action_items: Daniel Park (Redwood SE): Share retry/backoff samples + updated routing config - due 2026-04-27
Claire Thompson (Nimbus SRE): Run 24h load test at 1.2x and upload traces - due 2026-05-01
Maria Chen (Redwood AE): Send pricing impact estimate for dedicated capacity if needed - due 2026-04-29
transcript:
Header: 2026-04-24 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maria Chen, Daniel Park (Redwood); Claire Thompson, Ravi Patel, Lena Ortiz (Nimbus)

[00:00] Maria Chen: ok hi everyone thanks for jumping on, this is the weekly poc sync, main thing today is follow up on the flakiness from earlier this week, Claire do you want to kick off with what you saw?
[00:16] Claire Thompson: yeah uh thanks Maria. So on Monday between ~10:23 and 10:37 we saw a series of 5 5xx errors on the inference cluster, roughly 12 requests per minute, mostly long prompts. latency spiked then a bunch of client retries which made the load worse
[00:34] Ravi Patel: sorry just to clarify those are 5xx from your side or from redwood?
[00:40] Claire Thompson: they show up as 502/503 in our gateway logs, and the redwood responses had status 502 in the proxy traces. But also we saw a few client timeouts at 60s which then retried.
[00:58] Daniel Park: ok so two high-level things to look at: server-side transient errors, and retry amplification on the client. We pulled the Redwood runtime logs around those timestamps, saw a spike in kernel preemption and a few gpu stall messages — could be memory pressure from long sequence lengths plus batching.
[01:20] Lena Ortiz: we had a batch of 4k token generation tests that morning for the evaluation set that might have triggered it, yeah.
[01:28] Maria Chen: That matches — the POC config currently uses default batch size and the auto-batcher, so a sudden set of long sequences can cause longer GPU saturation windows. We can mitigate a few ways: cap max batch size for the route, or enable strict per-request token limit.
[01:46] Claire Thompson: also our client uses an aggressive retry with no jitter right now, it's basically immediate retries x3, which I think made the throughput worse.
[01:56] Daniel Park: yep that's classic. We recommend exponential backoff with jitter and capped retries. For this POC we suggest 2 retries with 250-500ms base then exponential up to 5s. We'll send sample config.
[02:14] Ravi Patel: what's the interaction with rate limits? We saw 429s later in the day once we throttled retries, curious if the token bucket is per-account or per-route.
[02:26] Daniel Park: today it's per-route for the hosted pilot, but if you move to dedicated capacity you get reserved qps and different limits. In hosted it's a combination: per-route soft limits plus account-level rate limit to protect cluster.
[02:42] Claire Thompson: can you explain why some of the errors were 5xx rather than 429?
[02:46] Daniel Park: couple possibilities — if the inference runtime exceeded a hard timeout or OOMed, kube proxy returns 502/503. 429s are when our rate limiter rejects requests before hitting the runtime. In your case we saw both: initial runtime failures then subsequent 429s once the gateway's token bucket engaged.
[03:06] Maria Chen: quick note — the auto-scaling policy for the dedicated stack is different; for hosted pilot we have stricter scaling thresholds to avoid noisy neighbor impact. If you expect big bursts we can simulate them in test env.
[03:20] Lena Ortiz: about tracing — can you enable request-level tracing for the pilot? The traces we pulled are missing KV cache hits and the prefix cache fields look garbled in our logs.
[03:32] Daniel Park: yes we can enable the higher-fidelity traces, we'll add the correlation IDs and an example dashboard link. Note traces increase log volume, but for troubleshooting it's very helpful.
[03:44] Claire Thompson: what's the recommended retry policy for streaming responses? Some of these are streaming so we saw partial events then disconnects.
[03:52] Daniel Park: for streaming the client should avoid blind retries on partial streams; do resume logic if you can, otherwise do a single retry with backoff and reconcile duplicates server-side if needed. We'll add a streaming guidance note.
[04:10] Ravi Patel: any thought on KV cache effect? earlier notes said prefix cache might have been bypassed.
[04:17] Daniel Park: in some cases long sequences and cache key mismatch can reduce cache hit rate; also if batching groups heterogeneous prefixes the prefix cache is less effective. We can tune batch grouping heuristics or enable conservative batching for your route.
[04:33] Maria Chen: we actually found one misconfiguration — the route for your pilot had a very high max_concurrent_requests which allowed many long-running requests to occupy slots; lowering that number reduced contention in our internal repro earlier.
[04:46] Claire Thompson: aha ok that could explain it. can you confirm what you changed?
[04:51] Daniel Park: we lowered max_concurrent_requests from 20 to 6 for the route and set max_batch_tokens to 8k. We also disabled cross-customer batching for that pool during the test.
[05:08] Lena Ortiz: did that reduce P99 latency?
[05:11] Daniel Park: in the repro it dropped P99 from ~3.2s to 1.6s for typical prompts, and the number of 5xx events in the repro went to zero. But we need your production-like load to be sure.
[05:24] Claire Thompson: ok good. next — rate limits and quotas: is there a short-term bump option? We hit 429s when retries started spiking.
[05:33] Maria Chen: for the POC we can temporarily raise the soft limit for your account or enable a burst multiplier for 30 minutes during the load test; we'll coordinate timing so it doesn't impact other tenants.
[05:44] Ravi Patel: sounds good. Also want to talk about alerting — we got paged by a noisy alert that marked a broad service outage; can we tune alert thresholds?
[05:53] Claire Thompson: yes the pagerduty rule fired on >5% 5xx in 5min which was too noisy for us, maybe a longer window or different metric would help.
[06:03] Daniel Park: we can propose adjusted alerting: use error budget + increase window to 10m and include runtime memory pressure metric correlation so it's higher fidelity.
[06:16] Maria Chen: quick note on retries again — avoid retrying on 5xx 500-series that indicate OOM; prefer retrying on 502/503 transient gateway errors with backoff. We'll add a short table in the guidance doc.
[06:30] Lena Ortiz: anything on the network path? our VPC peering could add a little jitter.
[06:36] Daniel Park: we'll do a network path deep-dive with your infra team; we suspect the egress NAT burst could cause SYN drops under heavy concurrency.
[06:47] Claire Thompson: ok good. Is there a recommended token bucket configuration on the client side? we saw spikes in concurrency from our batch worker.
[06:55] Daniel Park: yes use a leaky-bucket with steady refill, cap concurrency per worker to 4 and aggregate across workers with a shared rate limiter if possible. We'll share sample client code.
[07:07] Maria Chen: action items recap in a sec. Anything else before we move to schedule?
[07:11] Ravi Patel: one last question — if we switch to dedicated, do we still need the same retry policy?
[07:16] Daniel Park: you'll still want retries, but the thresholds change: dedicated has larger headroom and different rate limiting semantics; we'll provide a dedicated-specific config too.
[07:28] Claire Thompson: ok let's go over the timeline for tests. We'll run the 24h load from 04/28 to 04/29 at 1.2x, enable traces, and coordinate the temporary burst increase for 30 min at the start.
[07:43] Maria Chen: perfect. Daniel will send the retry doc and sample client config by Monday, and we'll enable tracing for the pilot. Maria will also send pricing for dedicated to Ravi.
[07:55] Daniel Park: sharing the link to the troubleshooting dashboard now (link: https://redwood.example.com/dashboards/nimbus-poc — sample). Also upload the repro logs we used to the shared drive.
[08:09] Claire Thompson: got it, thanks.

[08:15] Closing recap (Maria):
- root cause hypothesis: long sequence load + large batches -> memory pressure -> runtime errors + client retry amplification
- mitigations applied: lowered max_concurrent_requests, limited batch tokens, disabled cross-customer batching in repro
- immediate actions: enable tracing, share retry/backoff guidance, run extended load test with coordinated burst increase, tune alerts

[08:40] End meeting.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "KV cache 영향" from a stutter), speaker labels may be generic. Shared artifacts referenced: https://redwood.example.com/dashboards/nimbus-poc, shared drive repro logs (link: drive.google.com/drive/folders/example-repro-logs).
